title: expr~
description: evaluation of audio signal expressions on a vector by vector basis

messages.description: input to $f# or $i#, where # is the inlet number
result of an expression, one outlet per expression

arguments.description: expression including operators, functions, inlet types, float and symbols

body:
[expr~] evaluates C-like expressions on signals, vector by vector, combining signal and control processing. It works like [expr] with the addition of $v# for signal inputs, which is needed at least for the first inlet: "$v1" makes the first inlet a signal input. Inlets are defined by variables of the form $t#, where 't' is the type and # is the inlet number, counting from 1 at the left (up to 100): $f# is a float, $i# is an integer (floats are truncated) and $s# is a symbol, used for array names. Signal and control inlets can be mixed in any order.

The result is a signal. Multiple expressions separated by semicolons (up to 100) create one outlet each.

Arrays and variables (defined with [value]) are accessed as in C: "tab[5]" is element 5 of the array "tab", "$s2[5]" is element 5 of the array whose name came into inlet 2, and "valx + 10" adds 10 to the [value] named "valx". The store function "=" writes the result of an operation into a variable or array index, as in "tab[$f1] = $f2".

Besides the C operators (arithmetic, relational, bitwise and logical), the available functions are:
math: min, max, int, rint, round, trunc, nearbyint, float, abs, fmod, remainder, floor, ceil, modf, imodf, copysign, ldexp, hypot, if, random, isnan, isinf, finite
power and log: pow, sqrt, cbrt, exp, expm1, ln, log, log10, log1p, fact, erf, erfc
trigonometry: sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, sinh, cosh, tanh, asinh, acosh, atanh
tables: size, sum, Sum, avg, Avg
acoustics: mtof, ftom, dbtorms, rmstodb, dbtopow, powtodb
Functions that output a symbol only work in [expr].
